profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Google Gemini | Manhattan Community Board 3
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
👋 Hey there, I'm Zach! I am a full-stack software engineer with web, Android, data analysis, and iOS development experience. I have spent over six years working on language model products at Google -- in particular, Google Assistant and Gemini. I write code and prose daily to learn how complex systems work and build new features. I enjoy speaking to users directly to help them understand our products and find bugs. If you work at Google, you probably know me from my frequent posts on Memegen and Gemini-related chatrooms. 

Before becoming a software engineer, I spent five years in data science roles. A blog post I wrote in 2020 about data science interviewing sat atop of Hacker News for multiple days [1]. I have toyed around with the idea of becoming a founder in the past and have ranked in the top 10% of Y Combinator submissions for a past cohort.

Outside of work, since 2024 I have been a New York City civil servant with advocacy experience in housing, parks, and faith-based causes. You follow along my adventures in this arena through my newsletter, Friends of New York City Abundance [2]. 

[1] https://quip.com/2gwZArKuWk7W
[2] https://newyorkabundance.substack.com/

Past About summaries: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aQD7ztE1jUBFE01Zj4PwBrkPyooa4yyMQGdeIqUgD3Y

positions.title: Data Scientist
positions.description:
•	As Trailhead's first data scientist, wrote SQL defining user acquisition, retention, churn, cumulative lifetime metrics and other user behaviors. Created dashboards for business end users to easily access insights. 
•	Utilized AWS (EC2) to structure event log and user data of 2.2M+ rows to derive user behavior insights. Acted on insights to build collaborative filtering recommendation engine for website lessons. 
•	Automated plotting of weekly retention/cohort analysis by building Heroku web apps with Python.

positions.title: Data Scientist in Residence
positions.description:
•	Selected from 34 peers to be hired as math and statistics TA for Data Science Masters Program. 
•	Led twice-daily coding labs (1.5 hours each) for 18 students. Met w/students 1-on-1, held office hours. 
•	Graded daily labs/quizzes, conduct score reporting for two professors for positive student outcomes.

positions.title: Summer Program Leader
positions.description:
• Befriended with and oversaw group of 30+ Chinese high school students who wished to learn more about life at American colleges in a resident adviser-like role during week-and-a-half-long summer program in Shanghai, China. 
• Planned and led four student workshops about finding internships, creating a LinkedIn profile, American sports culture and college social life. 
• Chosen alongside six other interns attending Stanford (x2), Cornell, NYU, Brown and Dartmouth.

positions.title: Student Researcher/Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Research aide to Dr. Amanda Griffith, focusing on higher education. (Fall 2015)
Teaching Assistant to Dr. Staci White for MTH 358, Probability. (Spring 2016)
Research aide to Dr. Veronica Sovero, focusing on grade inflation. (Summer 2016)

positions.title: Data Science Intern
positions.description:
• Selected as the first data science team intern at growing customer acquisition and marketing company with partners in high growth industries. 
• Grew to become company leader in optimizing noncompliance detection using data science tools, communicating between different company teams and divisions. 
• Scripted with R programming language daily to clean data, build linear and logistic regression models, complete text mining using the TM package, and handle time-series data. 
• Employed MySQL and Pivot Tables in Microsoft Excel to obtain and analyze data.
• Utilized Linux shell to deploy scoring models live across company.

positions.title: Resident Adviser
positions.description:
• Developed community and promoted a positive residential experience as a student leader, policy resource, and counselor in hall of 24 upperclassmen residents.
• Organized monthly programming promoting service, healthy studying and cross-cultural interaction. Marketed programming to residents and filed appropriate reimbursement paperwork. 
• Completed weekly office hours, daily administrative tasks, and enforced policy in residence hall of 188 upperclassmen students.
• Collaborated with staff of five fellow resident advisers and the Graduate Hall Director to oversee residence hall operations.
• Following position vacancy, reemployed as a Resident Adviser in Magnolia Hall from March to May 2015.

positions.title: Community Service and Research Internship
positions.description:
Led or took part in specific projects for urban ministry in the Lower East Side, Manhattan:
• Advised organization on ongoing case management relief program after researching the Hurricane Sandy recovery in the region. 
• Planned and helped lead biweekly youth programming within New York City. 
• Developed curriculum for and co-taught weekly adult computer classes. 
• Organized trivia event and social for community residents.

positions.title: Student tutor
positions.description:
• Built math and reading skills with individual attention to elementary and middle school-aged children.
• Graded student work and aided with data management and recording.

projects.title: Industry Analysis of MOOCs
projects.description: Completed independent summer research project on massive open online courses (MOOCs) with funding from Joseph G. Gordon scholarship at Wake Forest. Attended April 2014 OpenCourseWare Consortium Global Conference in Ljubljana, Slovenia and personally completed two MOOCs for project. Sought to answer fundamental questions about MOOCs as part of career interest in higher education administration and public policy. Published findings on MOOCsMania.org.
